name: Fisher & Ury’s Principled Negotiation
diagnostic: Deadlocked discussions between Product Management and Engineering regarding scope vs. speed; engineers refusing to compromise on non-critical architectural preferences.

script.label: Interests vs. Positions Realignment
script.text: "We are locked in positional bargaining: Product demands a release by the 15th, and Engineering demands an additional month for testing. Let us decouple people from the problem. Product's underlying interest is meeting a client commitment; Engineering's underlying interest is preventing data loss in production. What delivery options fulfill both interests simultaneously?"

audit: Was the negotiated feature slice shipped on schedule with its agreed coverage?
Did Product and Engineering agree an objective release-gating metric?
auditFull: Was a negotiated feature slice deployed on schedule with agreed-upon test coverage?
Did Product and Engineering establish an objective metric for release gating?
foundation: Roger Fisher and William Ury’s Harvard Negotiation Project framework (Getting to Yes, 1981) focuses on four pillars: Separate the people from the problem; Focus on interests, not positions; Invent options for mutual gain; Insist on using objective criteria.

origin.title: Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In
